goal: Persist user and reviewer feedback as reusable shared agent guidance, and make the symlink-path unit test independent of Windows symlink privileges and sandbox temp paths.

in_scope: Add a repository-wide rule for recording user/reviewer feedback in the task worklog and promoting reusable process feedback into shared skills, QA checklists, or regression tests.
Update the module-pipeline and task-handoff skills to read relevant prior feedback, record dispositions, and carry reusable improvements forward.
Update the lesson-authoring skill so substantive lesson revisions include distinct independent review outputs and do not count author self-review as independent.
Change tests/test_taskctl.py to create fixtures under the repository's ignored .tmp directory and test the symlink-path guard without requiring host symlink-creation privilege.
Record the feedback disposition and test/environment findings in task-specific retrospective and validation reports.
out_of_scope: Changing taskctl.py path-validation behavior or relaxing its symlink rejection.
Editing provider-specific .codex/agents or .claude/agents profiles; shared procedures belong in .agents/skills.
Changing lesson content or modifying unrelated tests and modules.
Enabling Windows Developer Mode, administrator privileges, or other host settings.

constraints: Follow the repository's persistent task protocol and use @czyboi as the single writer.
Record task-specific feedback in the issue/worklog/report; promote only reusable process lessons into shared skills or regression checks.
Do not claim that a mocked unit test verifies the host operating system's symlink creation API; it verifies the repository's rejection branch deterministically.
Keep output paths unique and keep provider-specific profiles as thin role/configuration wrappers.

definition_of_done.text: AGENTS.md and shared skills describe where user/reviewer feedback is stored, how it is dispositioned, and when reusable feedback becomes a shared skill, checklist, or regression test; lesson-authoring directs substantive revisions to independent reviews.
TaskCtl test fixtures use a writable scratch directory under the workspace, and a non-skipped symlink-path guard unit test exercises relpath rejection without creating an OS symlink.
The content validator, complete unit suite, and task-state validator pass; results explain that the mocked guard test does not exercise Windows symlink creation.
The retrospective records the user's feedback, the prior workflow gap, the chosen durable feedback path, and the test's separate sandbox and OS-privilege causes.
All declared outputs are committed and task automation reaches automation_complete without inferring human approval.

acceptance_criteria.text: Future task instructions require relevant prior feedback to be read at intake, each new feedback item to have a recorded disposition, and reusable process changes to be committed to shared guidance with a regression check when practical.
For substantive lesson revisions, technical, pedagogical, and provenance/language review outputs are independently assigned as applicable; author self-review is never labelled independent.
The test fixture uses SOURCE_ROOT/.tmp as the TemporaryDirectory parent, avoiding the sandbox-restricted default temp location.
A deterministic unit test invokes taskctl.relpath with a symlink path component simulated through Path.is_symlink and asserts TaskError; it has no skip based on host symlink permissions.
No lesson, provider agent profile, or taskctl production behavior changes; the task report distinguishes unit guard coverage from a real OS symlink integration test.
python scripts/validate_content.py, python -m unittest discover -s tests -v, and python scripts/taskctl.py validate are recorded with exact outcomes.
